6. The respondent No.2 also filed an application under section 14 of the Limitation Act explaining the delay in filling the complaint case and prays	in for a condo nation of the same. 

 9. Thereafter the petitioner-corporation obtained the present Rule. Mr. Md. Nurul Huque, learned Advocate for the petitioner corporation-submits that the complaint case was barred by limitation and the Labour Court" was obviously outside its jurisdiction to entertain the same. 

 10. Section 25 (1) (b) provides that if the employer fails to give a decision under clause (a) or if the worker is dissatisfied with such decision, he may make a complaint to the Labour Court having jurisdiction, within thirty days from the last date under clause (a) or within thirty days from the date of the decision, as the case may be. Mr. Nurul Huque submits that 'the last order was passed on 23.1.83 and the respondent No.2 submitted the grievance petition on 18.3.83. Thereafter he filed Complaint Case No. 41 of 1983 in the Labour Court at Khulna with- in time. The Labour Court at Khulna returned the complaint case for filing in an appropriate Court by its order dated 24.4.84. Thereafter the respondent No. 2 filed the present complaint ease in the 2nd Labour Court at Dhaka on 16.6.84. The respondent No.2 has filed an application under section 14 of the Limitation Act and has stated that the time taken from 10.4.83 to 16.6.84 should be taken to have been spent in prosecuting the case with due diligence in another Court which from defect of jurisdiction was unable to entertain it. Mr. Nurul Haque submits that the Employment of Labour (Standing Orders) Act, 1965 being a special law Article 14 of the Limitation Act has no application. 

 11., This submission has no legs to stand. Section 29(2) of the Limitation Act provides as follows ;- " Where any special law prescribes for any suit, appeal or application a period of limitation different from the period prescribed therefor by the first schedule, the provision of section 3 shall apply, as if such period were prescribed therefor in that schedule, and for the purpose of determining any period of limitation prescribed for any suit, appear or' application by any special law - 

 Therefore Section 14 of the Limitation Act has full force and application and the 2nd Labour Court at Dhaka did not act without jurisdiction in entertaining the complaint case.
